title.en: Volume 125 Book of Later Zhou 27: Biographies 5 - Lie Chuanwu, Zhao Hui, Wang Shou'en, Kong Zhijun, Wang Jihong, Feng Hui, Gao Yunquan, Zhe Congruan, Wang Rao, Sun Fangjian
title.raw: 卷一百二十五 周書16: 列傳五 趙暉 王守恩 孔知濬 王繼弘 馮暉 高允權 折從阮 王饒 孫方諫 Volume 125 Book of Later Zhou 27: Biographies 5 - Lie Chuanwu, Zhao Hui, Wang Shou'en, Kong Zhijun, Wang Jihong, Feng Hui, Gao Yunquan, Zhe Congruan, Wang Rao, Sun Fangjian

sentences.zh: 趙暉，字重光，澶州人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Hui, style name Chongguang, was a man of Cazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hui, courtesy name Chongguang, was a native of Cazhou.

sentences.zh: 弱冠以驍果應募，始隸於莊宗帳前，與大梁兵經百餘戰，以功遷馬直軍使。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capping age he enlisted in the valiant cavalry, first attached to Emperor Zhuangzong's personal guard, fought the armies of Great Liang in more than a hundred battles, and was transferred to commissioner of the Imperial Horse Guard for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Upon coming of age he joined the elite cavalry corps and was first assigned to Emperor Zhuangzong's personal guard. After fighting the armies of Liang in more than a hundred engagements, he was promoted to commissioner of the Imperial Horse Guard for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 同光中，從魏王破蜀，命暉分統所部，南戍蠻陬。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era he followed the Prince of Wei in conquering Shu, was ordered to divide command of his troops, and garrisoned the southern barbarian frontier.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang period he accompanied the Prince of Wei in the conquest of Shu. He was then ordered to take independent command of his unit and garrison the southern frontier against the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，征還，授禁軍指揮使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he was recalled and appointed commander of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong acceded to the throne, Hui was recalled and appointed commander of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 晉有天下，參掌衛兵，從馬全節圍安陸，佐杜重威戰宗城，皆有功，改奉國指揮使。

translations.literal: When Jin held the realm he shared in commanding the guard troops, followed Ma Quanjie in besieging Anlu, assisted Du Chongwei in fighting at Zongcheng, all with merit, and was changed to commander of the Fengguo army.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin dynasty came to power, he helped command the palace guard. He served under Ma Quanjie in the siege of Anlu and assisted Du Chongwei at the battle of Zongcheng, distinguishing himself in both campaigns, and was then appointed commander of the Fengguo army.

sentences.zh: 開運末，以部兵屯於陜，屬契丹入汴，慨然有憤激之意。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyun era he stationed his troops at Shan, and when the Khitans entered Bian, he was stirred with indignant resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaiyun period he encamped his forces at Shan. When the Khitans entered Bian, he was filled with indignant resolve.

sentences.zh: 及聞漢祖建義於並門，乃與部將王晏、侯章戮力葉謀，逐契丹所命官屬，據有陜州，即時馳騎聞於漢祖。

translations.literal: When he heard that the Founder of Han had raised righteous arms at Bing Gate, he then with subordinate generals Wang Yan and Hou Zhang exerted joint effort in plotting, expelled the officials appointed by the Khitans, seized Shanzhou, and immediately sent riders to report to the Founder of Han.
translations.idiomatic: On learning that the Founder of Later Han had raised his banner at Bingzhou, he joined his subordinates Wang Yan and Hou Zhang in a concerted plot to drive out the officials the Khitans had installed, seize Shanzhou, and immediately dispatch riders to inform the founder.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：契丹主賜趙暉詔，即以為保義留後。

translations.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: The Khitan ruler bestowed an edict on Zhao Hui and immediately appointed him acting military commissioner of Baoyi.)
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Zizhi Tongjian》: The Khitan emperor issued an edict appointing Zhao Hui acting military commissioner of Baoyi.)

sentences.zh: 暉斬契丹使者，焚其詔，遣支使河間趙矩奉表晉陽。）〉

translations.literal: Hui beheaded the Khitan envoy, burned the edict, and sent administrative aide Zhao Ju of Hejian to present a memorial at Jinyang.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Hui executed the Khitan envoy, burned the edict, and sent his administrative aide Zhao Ju of Hejian to submit a memorial of allegiance at Jinyang.)〉

sentences.zh: 漢祖乃命暉為保義軍節度、陜虢等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: The Founder of Han then appointed Hui military commissioner of the Baoyi army and commissioner for observation and disposition of Shan, Guo, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The founder then appointed Hui military commissioner of the Baoyi army and commissioner overseeing Shan, Guo, and the surrounding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 漢祖之幸東京，路出於陜，暉戎服朝於路左，手控六飛達於行宮，君臣之義如舊結焉，旋加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When the Founder of Han visited the Eastern Capital, his route passed through Shan; Hui in military dress paid court on the left of the road, by hand guided the six steeds to reach the traveling palace, and the lord-and-minister bond was as of old ties; shortly he was additionally made acting grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder traveled to the Eastern Capital, his route passed through Shan. Hui met him on the roadside in full armor, took the reins of the imperial carriage and escorted it to the traveling palace, renewing their bond as sovereign and subject. He was soon given the additional title of acting grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，移鎮鳳翔，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was transferred to garrison Fengxiang and made associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qianyou era he was transferred to Fengxiang and given the title of associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 屬王景崇叛據岐山，及期不受代，朝廷即命暉為西南面行營都部署，統兵以討之。

translations.literal: When Wang Jingchong rebelled and held Qishan, and when his term expired would not accept replacement, the court immediately appointed Hui overall commander of the southwestern campaign headquarters and ordered him to lead troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingchong rebelled and seized Qishan and refused to step down at the end of his term, the court appointed Hui overall commander of the southwestern campaign and ordered him to lead an army against him.

sentences.zh: 時李守貞叛於蒲，趙思綰據於雍，與景崇皆遞相為援，又引蜀軍出自大散關，勢不可遏。

translations.literal: At that time Li Shouzhen rebelled at Pu, Zhao Sixian held Yong, and with Jingchong they mutually aided one another in turn; moreover they drew Shu troops out from Dasan Pass, and the momentum could not be checked.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Shouzhen had rebelled at Pu and Zhao Sixian held Yong; they and Jingchong supported one another in turn, while Shu forces advanced through Dasan Pass. The rebellion seemed unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 暉領兵數千，數戰而勝，然後塹而圍之。

translations.literal: Hui led several thousand troops, fought several times and won, then moated and besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui led several thousand men, won a series of engagements, and then dug trenches and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 暉屢使人挑戰，賊終不出，乃潛使千餘人，於城南一舍之外，擐甲執兵，偽為蜀兵旗幟，循南山而下，詐令諸軍聲言川軍至矣。

translations.literal: Hui repeatedly sent men to challenge battle, but the rebels to the end would not come out; he then secretly sent more than a thousand men a lodge beyond the south wall, donned armor and took weapons, feigned Shu army banners and flags, followed the southern mountains down, and falsely ordered the armies to proclaim that Sichuan troops had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Hui repeatedly sent out challengers, but the rebels refused to sally forth. He then secretly dispatched more than a thousand men a short distance beyond the south wall, armed and armored, bearing banners in imitation of Shu troops, and marched them down from the southern hills while ordering his army to spread the false report that Shu reinforcements had arrived.

sentences.zh: 須臾，西南塵起，城中以為信，乃令數千人潰圍而出，以為應援，暉設伏而待，一鼓而盡殪之。

translations.literal: In a moment dust rose in the southwest; the city believed it and then ordered several thousand men to break the encirclement and come out as supposed reinforcement; Hui set ambush and waited, and at one drumbeat annihilated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Before long dust rose in the southwest. The garrison took the ruse for fact and sent several thousand men out through the siege lines to meet their supposed allies. Hui's ambush struck at a single drumbeat and slaughtered them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 自是景崇膽破，不復敢出。

translations.literal: From this Jingchong's courage was broken and he no longer dared come out.
translations.idiomatic: From that point Jingchong lost his nerve and dared not venture out again.

sentences.zh: 明年春，拔之，加檢校太保、兼侍中。

translations.literal: The next spring he captured it, and Hui was additionally made acting grand guardian and concurrent palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he took the city. Hui was given the additional titles of acting grand guardian and concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 國初，就加兼中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty he was at once additionally made concurrent director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Zhou dynasty he was further appointed concurrent director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年春，拜章請覲，詔從之，入朝授歸德軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third spring he submitted a memorial requesting an audience; an edict approved it, and on entering court he was appointed military commissioner of the Guide army.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he petitioned for an audience at court. The emperor granted his request, and on his arrival he was appointed military commissioner of the Guide army.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年，受代歸闕，以疾告老，授太子太師致仕，進封秦國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiande he accepted replacement and returned to the capital, reported illness and requested retirement, was granted Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with retirement, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiande he was relieved of command and returned to court. Citing illness, he requested retirement and was granted the title of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with permission to retire, and was advanced in rank to Duke of Qin.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於其第，年六十七。

translations.literal: Shortly he died at his residence, age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at his residence at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 制贈尚書令。

translations.literal: By decree he was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously awarded him the title of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王守恩，字保信，太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Shou'en, style name Baoxin, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shou'en, courtesy name Baoxin, was a native of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父建立，潞州節度使，封韓王，《晉書》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Wang Jianli was military commissioner of Luzhou, enfeoffed as Prince of Han; the 《Jin History》 has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Jianli had served as military commissioner of Luzhou and was enfeoffed as Prince of Han; his biography appears in the 《Jin History》.

sentences.zh: 守恩以門蔭，幼為內職，遷懷、衛二州刺史，後歷諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: Shou'en through hereditary privilege in youth held inner service posts, was transferred to prefect of Huai and Wei prefectures, and later passed through various guard generals.
translations.idiomatic: Through his family's privilege Shou'en entered palace service in his youth, later served as prefect of Huai and Wei, and eventually held a succession of posts as guard general.

sentences.zh: 開運末，契丹陷中原，守恩時因假告歸於潞。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun the Khitans overran the Central Plains; Shou'en at that time on leave returned to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaiyun period the Khitans overran the Central Plains. Shou'en was then on leave and returned to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 時潞州節度使張從恩懼契丹之盛，將朝於戎王。

translations.literal: At that time the military commissioner of Luzhou Zhang Cong'en feared the Khitans' strength and was about to pay court to the barbarian king.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner of Luzhou, Zhang Cong'en, fearing Khitan power, was preparing to submit to the Khitan emperor.

sentences.zh: 以守恩婚家，甚倚信之，乃移牒守恩，請權為巡檢使。

translations.literal: Because Shou'en was connected by marriage, he relied on and trusted him greatly, and therefore sent a dispatch to Shou'en requesting him to act as inspection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong'en was related to Shou'en by marriage and trusted him deeply. He sent a dispatch asking Shou'en to serve as acting inspection commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從恩既去，守恩以潞城歸於漢祖，仍盡取從恩之家財。

translations.literal: After Cong'en had gone, Shou'en surrendered Luzhou to the Founder of Han and moreover took all of Cong'en's household wealth.
translations.idiomatic: After Cong'en departed, Shou'en surrendered Luzhou to the founder of Later Han and seized all of Cong'en's family property for himself.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》云：從恩以副使趙行遷知留後，牒守恩權巡檢使，與高防佐之。

translations.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: Cong'en had deputy commissioner Zhao Xingqian act as acting regent, dispatched Shou'en as acting inspection commissioner, and had Gao Fang assist him.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 records: Cong'en left his deputy Zhao Xingqian in charge as acting regent, appointed Shou'en acting inspection commissioner, and assigned Gao Fang to assist him.)

sentences.zh: 高防與守恩謀，遣指揮使李萬超白晝率眾大噪，斬趙行遷，推守恩權知昭義留後。

translations.literal: Gao Fang plotted with Shou'en, sent commander Li Wanchao in broad daylight to lead the crowd in a great uproar, beheaded Zhao Xingqian, and pushed Shou'en as acting regent of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Fang conspired with Shou'en and sent the commander Li Wanchao to lead the troops in a daytime mutiny. Li beheaded Zhao Xingqian and installed Shou'en as acting regent of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 守恩殺契丹使者，舉鎮來降。

translations.literal: Shou'en killed the Khitan envoy and raised the whole commandery to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shou'en executed the Khitan envoy and surrendered the entire prefecture.

sentences.zh: 《宋史·李萬超傳》云：張從恩將棄城歸契丹，會前驍衛將軍王守恩服喪私第，從恩即委以後事遁去。

translations.literal: 《Song History》, Biography of Li Wanchao, says: Zhang Cong'en was about to abandon the city and return to the Khitans; it happened that former general of the Valiant Guard Wang Shou'en was observing mourning at his private residence, and Cong'en immediately entrusted him with subsequent affairs and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Song History》 biography of Li Wanchao states: Zhang Cong'en was about to abandon the city and submit to the Khitans. Wang Shou'en, formerly a general of the Valiant Guard, was then observing mourning at his home, and Cong'en entrusted him with affairs before fleeing.

sentences.zh: 及契丹使至，專領郡務，守恩遂無所預，萬超奮然謂其部下曰：「我輩垂餌虎口，茍延旦夕之命，今欲殺使保其城，非止逃生，亦足建勛業，汝曹能乎？

translations.literal: When the Khitan envoy arrived and exclusively held prefectural affairs, Shou'en then had no part in them; Wanchao spiritedly said to his subordinates: "We hang as bait in the tiger's mouth, barely prolonging life day to day; now if we wish to kill the envoy and hold the city, we not only escape death but also can establish merit—can you do it?"
translations.idiomatic: When a Khitan envoy arrived and took sole charge of the prefecture, Shou'en was shut out of power entirely. Wanchao roused his men and said, "We hang by a thread in the tiger's jaws, barely clinging to life from one day to the next. If we kill this envoy and hold the city, we will not only save ourselves but win glory as well. Will you follow me?"

sentences.zh: 」眾皆躍然喜曰：「敢不唯命。

translations.literal: " The crowd all leaped up joyfully and said: "We dare not but obey your command."
translations.idiomatic: " The men leaped up with one voice: "We await only your word."

sentences.zh: 」遂率所部大噪入府署，殺其使，推守恩為帥，列狀以聞。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led his troops in a great uproar into the government offices, killed the envoy, pushed Shou'en as commander, and submitted a memorial reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led his troops in a clamorous assault on the government offices, killed the envoy, installed Shou'en as commander, and sent a memorial reporting the deed.

sentences.zh: 漢祖從其請，乃命史宏肇統兵，先渡河至潞，見萬超，語之曰：「收復此州，公之力也，吾欲殺守恩，以公為帥，可乎？

translations.literal: The Founder of Han granted his request and then ordered Shi Hongzhao to command troops, first cross the river to Lu, see Wanchao, and say to him: "Recovering this prefecture was your strength; I wish to kill Shou'en and make you commander—is it acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: The founder approved the request and sent Shi Hongzhao with an army. Crossing the river first to Luzhou, Hongzhao met Wanchao and said, "Recovering this prefecture was your doing. I intend to kill Shou'en and make you commander. What say you?"

sentences.zh: 」萬超對曰：「殺契丹使以推守恩，蓋為社稷計耳，今若賊害於人，自取其利，非宿心也。

translations.literal: " Wanchao replied: "Killing the Khitan envoy to push Shou'en was for the sake of the state; now if we harm a man to take profit for ourselves, that is not our original intent."
translations.idiomatic: " Wanchao replied, "We killed the Khitan envoy and installed Shou'en for the sake of the realm. To murder him now for my own gain would betray everything we stood for."

sentences.zh: 」宏肇大奇之。）〉

translations.literal: " Hongzhao greatly marveled at him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Hongzhao was deeply impressed.)〉

sentences.zh: 漢祖即以守恩為昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: The Founder of Han immediately made Shou'en military commissioner of the Zhaoyi army.
translations.idiomatic: The founder promptly appointed Shou'en military commissioner of the Zhaoyi army.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，移鎮邠寧，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When Han held the realm he was transferred to garrison Binning and made associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: After Later Han secured the realm, he was transferred to Binning and given the title of associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，遷永興軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was transferred to military commissioner of the Yongxing army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qianyou era he was appointed military commissioner of the Yongxing army.

sentences.zh: 時趙思綰已據長安，乃改授西京留守。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Sixian already held Chang'an, so he was instead appointed western capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Sixian had already seized Chang'an, so Shou'en was reassigned as regent of the western capital instead.

sentences.zh: 守恩性貪鄙，委任群小，以掊斂為務，雖病廢殘癃者，亦不免其稅率，人甚苦之。

translations.literal: Shou'en by nature was greedy and base, entrusted petty men, made extortion his task, and even the sick, crippled, and maimed were not spared his tax levies; the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Shou'en was greedy and contemptible by nature. He entrusted power to petty men and made extortion his chief occupation. Even the sick, crippled, and disabled were not exempt from his taxes, and the people suffered bitterly under him.

sentences.zh: 洛都嘗有豪士，為二姓之會，守恩乃與伶人數輩夜造，自為賀客，因獲白金數笏而退。

translations.literal: The Luo capital once had a wealthy man who held a gathering of two surnames; Shou'en then with several actors went by night, himself acted as congratulatory guest, and thereby obtained several tablets of white gold before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man in Luoyang once held a banquet for two allied clans. Shou'en went there at night with several actors, presented himself as a congratulatory guest, and walked away with several ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 太祖回自河中，駐軍於洛陽，詔以白文珂代之，守恩甚懼。

translations.literal: The Taizu returned from Hezhong, stationed troops at Luoyang, and by edict had Bai Wenke replace him; Shou'en was very afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu returned from Hezhong and encamped at Luoyang, an edict appointed Bai Wenke to replace him. Shou'en was terrified.

sentences.zh: 而洛人有曾為守恩非理割剝者，皆就其第征其舊物，守恩一一償之。

translations.literal: But people of Luo who had once been unreasonably stripped by Shou'en all came to his residence to demand their former goods, and Shou'en repaid them one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Those in Luoyang whom he had once cheated through unjust exactions now came to his residence to demand the return of their property, and Shou'en paid them back one by one.

sentences.zh: 及赴闕，止奉朝請而已。

translations.literal: When he went to court he held only the post of court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to court he held no more than the nominal rank of court attendant.

sentences.zh: 乾祐末，既殺史宏肇等，漢少帝召群臣上殿以諭之，時守恩越班而揚言曰：「陛下今日始睡覺矣。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianyou, after Shi Hongzhao and others had been killed, the young emperor of Han summoned the ministers to the hall to instruct them; at that time Shou'en stepped across the ranks and proclaimed aloud: "Your Majesty has only just awakened today."
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Qianyou era, after Shi Hongzhao and the others had been killed, the young emperor of Later Han summoned the ministers to the hall to address them. Shou'en stepped out of line and shouted, "Your Majesty has only just woken up today."

sentences.zh: 」其出言鄙俚如此。

translations.literal: " His words were vulgar and coarse like this.
translations.idiomatic: " His speech was as crude and vulgar as this.

sentences.zh: 國初，授左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty he was appointed general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Zhou dynasty he was appointed general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，改右金吾衛上將軍，封許國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was changed to general of the Right Golden Crow Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiande era he was transferred to general of the Right Golden Crow Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，舁疾歸洛而卒。

translations.literal: In the second winter he was carried home ill to Luo and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year he was carried home to Luoyang in illness and died there.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：周高祖為樞密，鳳翔、永興、河中三鎮反，高祖帶職出討之，回戈路由洛陽。

translations.literal: (《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Zhou Gaozu was Bureau Director; Fengxiang, Yongxing, and Hezhong, the three commands, rebelled; Gaozu led his post out to suppress them, and the returning route passed through Luoyang.)
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: When Zhou Gaozu was director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the three commands of Fengxiang, Yongxing, and Hezhong rebelled. Gaozu led his troops out to suppress them, and his return march took him through Luoyang.)

sentences.zh: 時王守恩為留守，以使相自專，乘檐子迎高祖於郊外，高祖遙見大怒，且疾驅入於公館。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shou'en was regent; he acted on his own as commissioner and chancellor, rode a sedan chair to welcome Gaozu in the suburbs; Gaozu saw from afar and was greatly angry, and moreover spurred swiftly into the guest house.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shou'en was then regent of Luoyang. Acting as though he were still a commissioner and chancellor in his own right, he rode out in a sedan chair to welcome Gaozu in the suburbs. Gaozu saw him from afar, flew into a rage, and spurred his horse straight into the guest residence.

sentences.zh: 久之，始令人傳旨，托以方浴，守恩不知其怒，但安坐俟久。

translations.literal: After a long while he first sent someone to convey an order, using the excuse that he was bathing; Shou'en did not know of his anger and only sat at ease waiting a long time.
translations.idiomatic: A long while passed before he sent word that he was bathing and could not receive visitors. Shou'en, unaware of his fury, simply sat and waited.

sentences.zh: 時白文珂在高祖麾下，召而謂曰：「王守恩乘檐子俟吾，誠無禮也，安可久為留守，汝宜亟去代之。

translations.literal: At that time Bai Wenke was under Gaozu's command; he summoned him and said: "Wang Shou'en rode a sedan chair to wait for me—truly without propriety; how can he long remain regent? You should quickly go replace him."
translations.idiomatic: Bai Wenke was then serving under Gaozu. Gaozu summoned him and said, "Wang Shou'en sat in a sedan chair waiting for me—that was grossly improper. He cannot remain regent. Go at once and replace him."

sentences.zh: 」文珂不敢違，於是即時禮上。

translations.literal: " Wenke dared not disobey, and thereupon immediately performed the ceremony of assumption.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenke dared not refuse and immediately took office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，吏馳去報守恩曰：「白侍中受樞密命，為留守訖。

translations.literal: Shortly an official galloped off to report to Shou'en: "Vice Director Bai received the Bureau Director's order and has become regent."
translations.idiomatic: Before long an official galloped to Shou'en and reported, "Vice Director Bai has received the Bureau Director's order and is now regent."

sentences.zh: 」留恩大驚，奔馬而歸，但見家屬數百口皆被逐於通衢中，百姓莫不聚觀。

translations.literal: " Shou'en was greatly startled, galloped home, and only saw several hundred family members all driven out into the main thoroughfare; common people all gathered to watch.
translations.idiomatic: " Shou'en was thunderstruck. He galloped home only to find several hundred members of his household driven out into the main street while crowds of onlookers gathered to watch.

sentences.zh: 其亦有乘便號叫索取貸錢物者。

translations.literal: There were also those who seized the opportunity to shout and demand repayment of loaned money and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Some took the occasion to shout demands for repayment of money and goods he owed them.

sentences.zh: 高祖使吏籍其數，立命償之，家財為之一空。

translations.literal: Gaozu had officials register the amounts and immediately ordered repayment; his household wealth was thereby emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had officials tally every claim and ordered immediate payment. Shou'en's household wealth was emptied in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 朝廷悚然，不甚為理。）〉

translations.literal: The court was startled and did not much pursue the matter.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The court was shaken but did little to intervene.)〉

sentences.zh: 孔知濬，字秀川，徐州滕縣人。

translations.literal: Kong Zhijun, style name Xiuchuan, was a man of Teng county, Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhijun, courtesy name Xiuchuan, was a native of Teng County in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太子太師致仕之猶子也。

translations.literal: He was the nephew by a younger brother of the retired Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was the nephew of a retired Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 父延緘，左武衛大將軍致仕，年九十餘卒。

translations.literal: His father Yanqian was a retired great general of the Left Martial Guard and died in his nineties.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanqian had retired as great general of the Left Martial Guard and died in his nineties.

sentences.zh: 知濬仕梁為天興軍使。

translations.literal: Zhijun served Liang as commissioner of the Tianxing army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun served the Liang dynasty as commissioner of the Tianxing army.

sentences.zh: 同光末，鎮昭義，時莊宗用唐朝故事，以黃門為監軍，皆恃恩暴橫，節將不能制。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongguang he garrisoned Zhaoyi; at that time Emperor Zhuangzong used Tang dynasty precedent, appointing eunuchs as army supervisors; all relied on favor and were violent and overbearing, and the military commissioners could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tongguang era he was posted to Zhaoyi. Emperor Zhuangzong had revived the Tang practice of appointing eunuchs as army supervisors. They abused imperial favor and ruled with violence, and the military commissioners could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 明宗鄴城之變，諸鎮多殺監軍。

translations.literal: In Emperor Mingzong's Ye City upheaval, many commands killed their army supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: During the upheaval at Ye City under Emperor Mingzong, commanders across the realm killed their army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 時監潞者懼誅，欲誘鎮兵謀變，知濬伏甲於室，淩晨監軍來謁，執而殺之，軍城遂寧。

translations.literal: At that time the supervisor at Lu feared execution and wished to entice the garrison troops into plotting rebellion; Zhijun hid armed men in his chamber; at dawn the army supervisor came to pay a visit, and he seized and killed him; the army city was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor at Luzhou, fearing execution, tried to incite the garrison to mutiny. Zhijun hid armed men in his chamber. At dawn, when the supervisor came to call on him, he seized and killed him, and the garrison was pacified.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘉之，洎罷鎮，以知濬為澤州刺史，入為左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong commended this; when he left the command he made Zhijun prefect of Ze and entered court as great general of the Left Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong praised his action. When Zhijun left his command, the emperor appointed him prefect of Ze and then summoned him to court as great general of the Left Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 長興、清泰中，歷唐、復、成三郡刺史。

translations.literal: In Changxing and Qingtai he successively served as prefect of Tang, Fu, and Cheng commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing and Qingtai periods he served in turn as prefect of Tang, Fu, and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖即位，用為奉國右廂都指揮使，領舒州刺史，從征範延光於鄴，遷宿州團練使，俄改隴州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne he employed him as commander of the right wing of the Fengguo army, concurrently prefect of Shu, followed the campaign against Fan Yanguang at Ye, was transferred to regimental commissioner of Suzhou, and shortly changed to defense commissioner of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu took the throne he appointed Zhijun commander of the right wing of the Fengguo army and concurrent prefect of Shu. He accompanied the campaign against Fan Yanguang at Ye, was then made regimental commissioner of Suzhou, and soon after transferred to defense commissioner of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 開運中，移刺鳳州，累官至檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In Kaiyun he was transferred to govern Feng prefecture and rose through accumulated offices to acting grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyun period he was transferred to Fengzhou and rose through successive promotions to acting grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 河池據關防之要，密邇邛、蜀，兵少勢孤，知濬撫士得宜，人皆盡力，故西疆無牧圉之失。

translations.literal: Hechi occupied the key to passes and defenses, close to Qiong and Shu; troops were few and the position isolated; Zhijun comforted the soldiers appropriately and all exerted their strength, so the western frontier had no loss of herds and pastures.
translations.idiomatic: Hechi occupied a critical pass on the frontier, close to Qiong and Shu. With few troops in an isolated post, Zhijun treated his men well and won their full effort, so the western border suffered no loss of herds to raiders.

sentences.zh: 契丹主稱制，署滑州節度使。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler claimed the regency he appointed him military commissioner of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor assumed control of the Central Plains, he appointed Zhijun military commissioner of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 漢祖受命，自鎮入朝。

translations.literal: When the Founder of Han received the Mandate he came from his command to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Later Han took power, Zhijun left his post and went to court.

sentences.zh: 隱帝嗣位，授密州防禦使，逾歲，以疾受代歸朝。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded he was appointed defense commissioner of Mizhou; after more than a year, on illness he accepted replacement and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded to the throne, Zhijun was appointed defense commissioner of Mizhou. After a year he fell ill, was relieved of command, and returned to court.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年冬，卒於京師。

translations.literal: In the third winter of Guangshun he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Guangshun he died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 王繼宏，冀州南宮人。

translations.literal: Wang Jihong, a man of Nangong in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jihong was a native of Nangong in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 少嘗為盜，攻剽閭裏，為吏所拘，械系於鎮州獄，會赦免死，配隸本軍，時明宗作鎮，致之麾下。

translations.literal: In youth he had been a bandit, raiding villages and lanes, was seized by officials, shackled and imprisoned in Zhenzhou jail; he met an amnesty and escaped death, was assigned to serve in the local army; at that time Emperor Mingzong held the command and brought him under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he had been a bandit who raided the countryside. Officials arrested him and chained him in the prison at Zhenzhou. An amnesty spared his life, and he was assigned to the local army. Emperor Mingzong, then holding the command, took him into his service.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖為明宗將，署為帳中小校。

translations.literal: Jin Gaozu was then Mingzong's general and appointed him a junior officer in the headquarters guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu was still a general under Mingzong, he appointed Jihong a junior officer in his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 天福中，為六宅副使。

translations.literal: In Tianfu he was deputy commissioner of the Six Residences.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu period he served as deputy commissioner of the Six Residences.

sentences.zh: 性負氣不遜，禁中與同列忿爭，出配義州軍。

translations.literal: By nature he was proud and insubordinate; in the palace he quarreled angrily with colleagues and was sent out to serve with the Yizhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and insubordinate by nature, he quarreled with colleagues in the palace and was reassigned to the army at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為奉國指揮使，從契丹主至相州，遂令以本軍戍守。

translations.literal: After more than a year he became commander of the Fengguo army, followed the Khitan ruler to Xiangzhou, and was then ordered to garrison with his original army.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was made commander of the Fengguo army. He accompanied the Khitan emperor to Xiangzhou and was ordered to garrison the city with his troops.

sentences.zh: 契丹主留高唐英為相州節度使。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler left Gao Tangying as military commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor left Gao Tangying as military commissioner of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐英善待繼宏，每候其第，則升堂拜繼宏之母，贈遺甚厚，倚若親戚，又給以兵仗，略無猜忌。

translations.literal: Tangying treated Jihong well; each time he called at his residence he would ascend the hall and bow to Jihong's mother, gave generous gifts, relied on him as kin, and moreover supplied weapons and gear, with scarcely any suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Tangying treated Jihong with great kindness. Whenever he called at his residence he would enter the hall and bow to Jihong's mother, lavished gifts upon them, relied on him as though he were family, and even supplied him with arms and equipment, scarcely suspecting him at all.

sentences.zh: 會契丹主死，漢祖趨洛，唐英遣使歸款，漢祖大悅，將厚待唐英。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler died and the Founder of Han hurried to Luo, Tangying sent envoys to submit allegiance; the Founder was greatly pleased and was about to treat Tangying generously.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor died and the founder of Later Han marched on Luoyang, Tangying sent envoys to submit. The founder was delighted and prepared to reward him generously.

sentences.zh: 使未回，繼宏與指揮使樊暉等共殺唐英，繼宏自稱留後，令判官張易奉表於漢祖。

translations.literal: Before the envoys returned, Jihong with commander Fan Hui and others jointly killed Tangying; Jihong declared himself acting regent and ordered administrative aide Zhang Yi to present a memorial to the Founder of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoys returned, Jihong joined the commander Fan Hui and others in killing Tangying. Jihong declared himself acting regent and ordered his administrative aide Zhang Yi to submit a memorial of allegiance to the founder.

sentences.zh: 人或責以見利忘義，繼宏曰：「吾儕小人也，若不因利乘便，以求富貴，畢世以來，未可得志也。

translations.literal: Some reproached him for seeing profit and forgetting righteousness; Jihong said: "We are petty men; if we do not seize advantage when profit offers itself to seek wealth and honor, through a whole lifetime we could not have achieved our ambition."
translations.idiomatic: When some reproached him for betraying a benefactor for gain, Jihong said, "We are base men. If we do not seize every chance fortune offers to win wealth and rank, we may live out our whole lives without ever fulfilling our ambitions."

sentences.zh: 」及漢祖征杜重威至德清軍，繼宏來朝，乃正授節旄。

translations.literal: " When the Founder of Han campaigned against Du Chongwei to Deqing army, Jihong came to court and was then formally granted the military commissioner's banner.
translations.idiomatic: " When the founder marched against Du Chongwei as far as Deqing, Jihong came to court and was formally invested with the commissioner's insignia.

sentences.zh: 是歲，就加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: That year he was at once additionally made acting grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was given the additional title of acting grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 節度判官張易，每見繼宏不法，必切言之，繼宏以為輕己。

translations.literal: The military commissioner's administrative aide Zhang Yi, whenever he saw Jihong's unlawful conduct, always spoke sharply; Jihong thought he slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: His administrative aide Zhang Yi rebuked Jihong sharply whenever he saw him break the law. Jihong took this as a personal insult.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，因事誣奏殺之，尋又害觀察推官張制。

translations.literal: In Qianyou, on a pretext he submitted a false accusation and had him killed; shortly he also harmed investigation aide Zhang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou period he fabricated charges and had Zhang Yi executed, and soon afterward killed the investigation aide Zhang Zhi as well.

sentences.zh: 漢末，移鎮貝州，就加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: At the end of Han he was transferred to garrison Beizhou and was at once additionally made acting grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Han dynasty he was transferred to Beizhou and given the additional title of acting grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was additionally made associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangshun era he was given the title of associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，移鎮河陽，會永壽節入覲，遇疾卒於京師，詔贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year he was transferred to garrison Heyang; when the Eternal Longevity festival came he entered court for an audience, met illness and died in the capital; by edict he was posthumously granted Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year he was transferred to Heyang. When he came to court for the Eternal Longevity festival he fell ill and died in the capital. An edict posthumously awarded him the title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子永昌，仕皇朝，歷內諸司使。

translations.literal: His son Yongchang served the imperial dynasty and passed through various inner bureau commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongchang served the Zhou court in a succession of posts as inner bureau commissioner.

sentences.zh: 馮暉，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Feng Hui was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 始為效節軍士，拳勇騎射，行伍憚之，初事楊師厚為隊長。

translations.literal: He first was a soldier of the Loyalty army, fierce in boxing and skilled in mounted archery; the ranks feared him; he first served Yang Shihou as squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a soldier in the Loyalty army, renowned for his prowess in hand-to-hand combat and mounted archery. His comrades feared him. He first served under Yang Shihou as a squad leader.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，以銀槍效節為親軍，與梁人對壘河上，暉以犒給稍薄，因竄入南軍，梁將王彥章置之麾下。

translations.literal: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei, the Silver Spear Loyalty troops were his personal guard; facing the Liang armies across the river, Hui because rewards were somewhat meager thereupon fled into the southern army; Liang general Wang Yanzhang placed him under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Wei, the Silver Spear Loyalty troops served as his personal guard. Stationed opposite the Liang armies on the Yellow River, Hui found the rations and rewards too meager and defected to the southern forces. The Liang general Wang Yanzhang took him into his command.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平河南，暉首罪，赦之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Henan, Hui confessed his crime first and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified Henan, Hui was the first to confess his crime and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 從明宗征潞州，誅楊立有功。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Mingzong in campaigning against Luzhou and had merit in executing Yang Li.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Emperor Mingzong in the campaign against Luzhou and distinguished himself in the execution of Yang Li.

sentences.zh: 又從魏王繼岌伐蜀，蜀平，授夔州刺史。

translations.literal: He again followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in attacking Shu; when Shu was pacified he was appointed prefect of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in the conquest of Shu. After Shu was pacified he was appointed prefect of Kui.

sentences.zh: 時荊州高季興叛，以兵攻其城，暉拒之，屢敗荊軍。

translations.literal: At that time Jingzhou's Gao Jixing rebelled and with troops attacked his city; Hui resisted him and repeatedly defeated the Jing armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jixing of Jingzhou rebelled and attacked his city with an army, Hui held him off and repeatedly defeated the Jing forces.

sentences.zh: 長興中，為興州刺史，以乾渠為治所。

translations.literal: In Changxing he was prefect of Xingzhou and made Qianqu his seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing period he was made prefect of Xingzhou with his seat at Qianqu.

sentences.zh: 會兩川叛，蜀人來侵，暉以眾寡不敵，奔歸鳳翔，朝廷怒其失守，詔於同州衙職安置。

translations.literal: When the two Sichuan circuits rebelled and Shu people came to invade, Hui because his forces were too few to match the enemy fled back to Fengxiang; the court was angry at his loss of the post and by edict placed him in a Tongzhou yamen post.
translations.idiomatic: When the two Sichuan circuits rebelled and Shu forces invaded, Hui, outnumbered, fled to Fengxiang. The court, furious at his failure to hold his post, ordered him reassigned to a staff position at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，從晉高祖討蜀，蜀人守劍門，領部下兵逾越險阻，從他道出於劍門之左掩擊之，殺守兵殆盡。

translations.literal: Before long he followed Jin Gaozu in suppressing Shu; Shu men guarded Jianmen Pass; he led his subordinate troops over steep obstacles, by another route came out to the left of Jianmen and struck by surprise, killing the garrison troops nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he joined Jin Gaozu in the campaign against Shu. When Shu troops held Jianmen Pass, he led his men over treacherous terrain by a side route, emerged to the left of the pass, and launched a surprise attack that slaughtered the garrison almost to a man.

sentences.zh: 會晉祖班師，朝廷以暉為澶州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu withdrew the army, the court made Hui prefect of Cazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu withdrew his army, the court appointed Hui prefect of Cazhou.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，範延光據鄴叛，以暉為馬步都將，孫銳為監軍，自六明鎮渡河，將襲滑臺，尋為官軍所敗，暉退歸鄴，為延光城守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin Tianfu, Fan Yanguang held Ye in rebellion; he made Hui combined cavalry and infantry commander and Sun Rui army supervisor; from Liuming town they crossed the river intending to strike Huatai; shortly they were defeated by government troops; Hui retreated to Ye and defended the city for Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu period Fan Yanguang rebelled and seized Ye. He appointed Hui combined cavalry and infantry commander with Sun Rui as army supervisor. They crossed the river from Liuming town intending to strike Huatai but were soon defeated by imperial forces. Hui retreated to Ye and defended the city for Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，暉因出戰而降，授滑州節度使、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: The next autumn Hui because he went out to battle surrendered and was appointed military commissioner of Huazhou and acting grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Hui surrendered during a sortie from the city and was appointed military commissioner of Huazhou with the additional title of acting grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 鄴平，移鎮靈武。

translations.literal: When Ye was pacified he was transferred to garrison Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: After Ye was pacified he was transferred to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 初，張希崇鎮靈州，以久在蕃，頗究邊事，數年之間，侵盜並息。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Xichong garrisoned Lingzhou; because he had long been among the barbarians he thoroughly studied frontier affairs; within several years raids and plunder all ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Xichong had governed Lingzhou. Long service among the frontier peoples had given him deep knowledge of border affairs, and within a few years raids and plunder ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 希崇卒，未有主帥，蕃部寇鈔，無復畏憚，朝廷以暉強暴之名聞於遐僥，故以命之。

translations.literal: When Xichong died there was no commander; barbarian tribes raided and plundered without fear again; the court because Hui's name for violence was known in distant lands therefore appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: After Xichong died the post had no commander, and tribal raids resumed without restraint. The court appointed Hui because his reputation for ruthless force was known even in distant lands.

sentences.zh: 及暉到鎮，大張宴席，酒殽豐備，郡夷告醉，爭陳獻賀，暉皆以錦彩酬之，蕃情大悅。

translations.literal: When Hui reached his command he spread a great feast; wine and dishes were abundantly prepared; tribal chiefs of the prefecture declared themselves drunk and vied to present congratulations; Hui all rewarded them with brocades and silks; barbarian sentiment was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui reached his post he held a lavish feast with abundant food and wine. The tribal leaders drank their fill and competed to offer congratulations. Hui rewarded them all with brocades and silks, winning their hearts completely.

sentences.zh: 党項拓拔彥昭者，州界部族之大者，暉至來謁，厚加待遇，仍為治第，豐其服玩，因留之不令歸部。

translations.literal: The Tangut Tuo Ba Yanzhao was the greatest of the tribal groups within the prefecture's borders; when Hui arrived he came to pay a visit; Hui treated him generously, moreover built him a residence, enriched his clothing and ornaments, and thereby detained him and would not let him return to his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut leader Tuo Ba Yanzhao headed the largest tribal group in the region. When he came to pay his respects, Hui treated him with great honor, built him a fine residence, lavished gifts of clothing and ornaments upon him, and then detained him, refusing to let him return to his people.

sentences.zh: 河西羊馬，由是易為交市。

translations.literal: Hexi sheep and horses thereby became easy to trade in markets.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep and horses from the Hexi region thus became readily available for trade.

sentences.zh: 暉期年得馬五千匹，而蕃部歸心，朝議患之。

translations.literal: Within a year Hui obtained five thousand horses, and the barbarian tribes submitted in heart; court deliberation worried over this.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Hui acquired five thousand horses and won the wholehearted loyalty of the tribes. The court grew alarmed.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《隆平集·藥元福傳》：西戎三族攻靈州，命元福佐朔方節度使馮暉討之。

translations.literal: (《Longping Collection》, Biography of Yao Yuanfu: The three western Rong tribes attacked Lingzhou; Yuanfu was ordered to assist Shuofang military commissioner Feng Hui in suppressing them.)
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Longping Collection》, biography of Yao Yuanfu: Three western tribal groups attacked Lingzhou, and Yuanfu was ordered to assist the Shuofang military commissioner Feng Hui in suppressing them.)

sentences.zh: 朔方距威州七百里，地無水草，謂之「旱海」。

translations.literal: Shuofang was seven hundred li from Weizhou; the land had no water or grass and was called the "Dry Sea."
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang lay seven hundred li from Weizhou across a waterless, grassless expanse known as the Dry Sea.

sentences.zh: 攜糧至，暉食盡，詰朝行四十里，而敵騎數萬扼要路。

translations.literal: They carried provisions there; Hui's food was exhausted; at dawn they marched forty li, but enemy cavalry in the tens of thousands held the critical road.
translations.idiomatic: They carried provisions with them, but Hui's supplies ran out. At dawn they marched forty li only to find tens of thousands of enemy horsemen blocking the vital route ahead.

sentences.zh: 暉大懼，遣人致賂求成，雖許，及日中猶未決。

translations.literal: Hui was greatly afraid, sent men to offer bribes and seek peace; although they agreed, by midday it was still undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was terrified and sent envoys with bribes to negotiate peace. Though the enemy agreed in principle, by midday no settlement had been reached.

sentences.zh: 暉曰：「奈何？

translations.literal: Hui said: "What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "What are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 」元福曰：「彼正欲困我耳，察其勢，敵雖眾，特依西山而陣者，其精兵也，請以驍銳先薄西山，彼或少怯，當舉黃旗為識。

translations.literal: " Yuanfu said: "They precisely wish to wear us down. Observing their disposition, though the enemy is numerous, those who rely especially on the western hills in formation are their elite troops. Please use valiant sharp troops first to press the western hills; if they show a little fear, you should raise a yellow banner as the signal."
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanfu replied, "They mean to wear us down. Look at their disposition: though numerous, their elite troops are those arrayed along the western hills. Send your best fighters to strike the hills first. If they falter even slightly, raise a yellow banner as our signal."

sentences.zh: 」暉善其謀，斬馘殆盡。）〉

translations.literal: " Hui approved his plan and beheaded and ear-collected the enemy nearly to the last man.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Hui approved the plan and slaughtered the enemy almost to the last man.)〉

sentences.zh: 晉開運初，桑維翰輔政，欲圖大舉以制北方，命將佐十五人，皆列藩之帥也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin Kaiyun, Sang Weihan assisted in government and wished to plan a great campaign to control the north; he ordered fifteen generals and aides, all commanders of frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyun period Sang Weihan held power and planned a major northern campaign. He named fifteen generals, all of them frontier commanders.

sentences.zh: 惟暉不預其數，乃上章自陳，且言未老可用，而制書見遺。

translations.literal: Only Hui was not included in the number; he therefore submitted a memorial stating himself, and moreover said he was not yet old and could be used, yet the imperial order overlooked him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui alone was left off the list. He submitted a memorial protesting that he was not yet too old for service and had been unjustly passed over.

sentences.zh: 詔報云：「非制書忽忘，實以朔方重地，蕃部窺邊，非卿雄名，何以彈壓！

translations.literal: The edict in reply said: "It is not that the imperial order forgot you; truly because Shuofang is a weighty region and barbarian tribes watch the border, without your formidable name, how could we suppress them!"
translations.idiomatic: The imperial reply read: "You were not forgotten. Shuofang is a critical post, and the tribes along the border are watching. Without your formidable reputation, who could hold them in check?"

sentences.zh: 比欲移卿內地，受代亦須奇才。

translations.literal: Recently we wished to move you to the interior, but to receive your replacement also requires an extraordinary talent."
translations.idiomatic: We have wished to bring you inland, but finding a worthy successor for Shuofang requires an extraordinary man."

sentences.zh: 」暉得詔甚喜，又達情乞移鎮邠州，即以節鉞授之。

translations.literal: " Hui received the edict and was very pleased; he also conveyed his wish begging transfer to garrison Binzhou, and was immediately granted the military commissioner's insignia.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui was delighted by the edict and petitioned to be transferred to Binzhou, which was granted immediately along with the commissioner's insignia.

sentences.zh: 行未及邠，又除陜州，暉獻馬千匹、駝五百頭。

translations.literal: Before he had reached Bin he was again appointed to Shanzhou; Hui presented a thousand horses and five hundred camels.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Binzhou he was reassigned to Shanzhou. Hui presented a thousand horses and five hundred camels as tribute.

sentences.zh: 在陜未幾，除侍衛步軍都指揮使，兼領河陽，即以王令溫為靈武節度使。

translations.literal: At Shan not long after he was made commander of the palace guard infantry, concurrently holding Heyang; Wang Lingwen was immediately made military commissioner of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: After a short stay at Shanzhou he was appointed commander of the palace guard infantry and given concurrent command of Heyang. Wang Lingwen was appointed military commissioner of Lingwu in his place.

sentences.zh: 暉既典禁兵，兼領近鎮，為朝廷縻留，頗悔離靈武。

translations.literal: Hui having charge of the forbidden troops and concurrently holding a nearby command, was detained by the court and greatly regretted leaving Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Now commanding the palace guard and a nearby command, Hui was kept at court and deeply regretted leaving Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 及馮玉、李彥韜用事，暉善奉之，未幾，復以暉為朔方節度使，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: When Feng Yu and Li Yantao held power, Hui skillfully served them; before long Hui was again made Shuofang military commissioner and given the additional title of acting grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Yu and Li Yantao came to power, Hui cultivated them assiduously. Before long he was restored to the Shuofang command with the additional title of acting grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖革命，就加同平章事。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu carried out the revolution he was at once additionally made associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Han Gaozu seized power, Hui was given the additional title of associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 隱帝嗣位，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded he was additionally made concurrent palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded to the throne, Hui was given the additional title of concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 國初，加中書令，封陳留王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty he was made director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Zhou dynasty he was made director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Prince of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年夏，病卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the third summer of Guangshun he died of illness, age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year of Guangshun he died of illness at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 追贈衛王。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 子繼業，朔方衙內都虞候。

translations.literal: His son Jiye was overall adjutant within the Shuofang yamen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiye served as overall adjutant of the Shuofang headquarters.

sentences.zh: 暉亡，三軍請知軍府事，因授檢校太保，充朔方兵馬留後。

translations.literal: When Hui died the three armies requested that he manage military headquarters affairs; he was therefore granted acting grand guardian and made acting Shuofang military regent.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's death the army asked Jiye to take charge of headquarters affairs. He was appointed acting grand guardian and acting Shuofang military regent.

sentences.zh: 皇朝乾德中，移於內地，今為同州節度使。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era of the imperial dynasty he was moved to the interior; he is now military commissioner of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande era of the Song dynasty he was transferred inland and now serves as military commissioner of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 高允權，延州人。

translations.literal: Gao Yunquan was a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yunquan was a native of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖懷遷，本郡牙將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huaiqian was a yamen general of the native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huaiqian had been a yamen general of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 懷遷生二子，長曰萬興，次曰萬金，梁、唐之間為延州節度使，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: Huaiqian bore two sons; the elder was called Wanxing, the younger Wanjin; between Liang and Tang they were military commissioners of Yanzhou and died in their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiqian had two sons, the elder Wanxing and the younger Wanjin. Between the Liang and Tang dynasties they served in turn as military commissioners of Yanzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 允權即萬金子也。

translations.literal: Yunquan was Wanjin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yunquan was the son of Wanjin.

sentences.zh: 雖出於將門，不嫻武藝，起家為義川主簿，歷膚施縣令，罷秩歸延州之第。

translations.literal: Although he came from a general's house he was not skilled in martial arts; he began his career as registrar of Yichuan, passed through magistrate of Fushi county, left office and returned to his residence at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Though born into a military family, he had no skill in arms. He began as registrar of Yichuan, served as magistrate of Fushi County, and then retired to his family estate at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，以周密為延帥，延有東西二城，其中限以深澗。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin Kaiyun, Zhou Mi was made Yan commander; Yan had eastern and western two cities, between which a deep ravine served as boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaiyun period Zhou Mi was appointed commander of Yanzhou. The prefecture had eastern and western cities separated by a deep ravine.

sentences.zh: 及契丹入汴，一日，州兵亂，攻密，密固守東城。

translations.literal: When the Khitans entered Bian, one day the prefectural troops mutinied and attacked Mi; Mi firmly held the eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans entered Bian, the prefectural troops mutinied one day and attacked Zhou Mi, who held fast in the eastern city.

sentences.zh: 亂兵既無帥，亦無敢為帥者，或曰：「取高家西宅郎君為帥可也。

translations.literal: The mutinous troops had no commander and none dared be commander; someone said: "Taking the young master of the Gao family's western residence as commander would do."
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers had no leader and no one dared claim command. Someone said, "We should make the young master of the Gao family's western residence our commander."

sentences.zh: 」是夜未曙，允權方寢，亂軍排闥，請知留後事，遂居於西城，與密相拒數日。

translations.literal: " That night before dawn Yunquan was just sleeping; the mutinous army broke the door and requested that he manage acting regent affairs; he thereupon dwelt in the western city and opposed Mi for several days.
translations.idiomatic: " That night before dawn, while Yunquan was still asleep, the mutineers broke down his door and asked him to take charge as acting regent. He occupied the western city and held Zhou Mi at bay for several days.

sentences.zh: 河東遣供奉官陳光穗宣撫河西，允權乃遣支使李彬奉表太原，周密棄東城而去。

translations.literal: Hedong sent tribute commissioner Chen Guangsu to proclaim and soothe Hexi; Yunquan then sent administrative aide Li Bin to present a memorial at Taiyuan; Zhou Mi abandoned the eastern city and left.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong sent the tribute commissioner Chen Guangsu to pacify the Hexi region. Yunquan dispatched his administrative aide Li Bin to submit a memorial at Taiyuan. Zhou Mi abandoned the eastern city and fled.

sentences.zh: 漢祖遣使就加允權檢校太傅，仍正授旄鉞。

translations.literal: The Founder of Han sent envoys to add for Yunquan the title of acting grand mentor on the spot, and still formally grant the military commissioner's banner and axe.
translations.idiomatic: The founder of Later Han sent envoys to appoint Yunquan acting grand mentor and formally invest him with the commissioner's insignia.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，允權屢修貢奉。

translations.literal: When the Founder of Han entered Bian, Yunquan repeatedly sent tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: After the founder entered Bian, Yunquan sent tribute repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，加檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor took the throne he was given acting grand marshal and associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded to the throne, Yunquan was given the titles of acting grand marshal and associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 允權與夏州李彜興不協，其年李守貞據河中叛，密構彜興為援，及朝廷用兵夏州，軍逼延州，允權上章論列，彜興亦紛然自訴，朝廷賜詔和解之。

translations.literal: Yunquan was not in harmony with Xiazhou's Li Yiying; that year Li Shouzhen held Hezhong in rebellion and secretly enlisted Yiying as aid; when the court used troops against Xiazhou the army pressed Yanzhou; Yunquan submitted a memorial arguing the case; Yiying also clamorously pleaded his own case; the court bestowed an edict to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: Yunquan was on bad terms with Li Yiying of Xiazhou. That year Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and secretly sought Yiying's support. When imperial forces marched on Xiazhou and approached Yanzhou, Yunquan submitted a memorial of protest and Yiying lodged complaints of his own. The court issued an edict commanding reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 太子太師致仕劉景巖，允權妻之祖也，退老於州之別墅。

translations.literal: Retired Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Liu Jingyan was Yunquan's wife's grandfather and retired to old age at a villa in the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingyan, a retired Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Yunquan's wife's grandfather, lived in retirement at a villa in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景巖舊事高氏為牙校，亦嘗為延帥，甚得民心。

translations.literal: Jingyan formerly served the Gao clan as yamen officer and had also once been Yan commander; he greatly won the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyan had once served the Gao clan as a yamen officer and had himself been commander of Yanzhou. He enjoyed great popular support.

sentences.zh: 景巖以允權婚家後輩，心輕之。

translations.literal: Jingyan because Yunquan was a junior of the marriage family inwardly looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyan looked down on Yunquan as a junior connected by marriage.

sentences.zh: 允權恒忌其強，是歲冬，盡殺景巖之家，收其家財萬計，以謀叛聞，朝廷不能辨。

translations.literal: Yunquan constantly resented his strength; that winter he killed all of Jingyan's household, seized his household wealth numbering in the tens of thousands, reported it as plotting rebellion, and the court could not distinguish truth.
translations.idiomatic: Yunquan constantly resented his influence. That winter he slaughtered Jingyan's entire household, seized wealth amounting to tens of thousands, and reported the deed as suppression of a rebellion. The court could not tell otherwise.

sentences.zh: 關西賊平，方面例覃恩命，就加允權檢校太師。

translations.literal: When the Guanxi rebels were pacified, frontier regions by precedent received grace edicts; Yunquan was at once additionally made acting grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels in the western passes were pacified, frontier commanders customarily received imperial favors. Yunquan was given the additional title of acting grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne he was additionally made concurrent palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Yunquan was given the additional title of concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年春卒，其子紹基匿喪久之，又擅主軍政，欲邀承襲。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Guangshun he died; his son Shaoji concealed the death a long time, moreover usurped control of military affairs, and wished to invite succession.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the spring of the third year of Guangshun. His son Shaoji concealed the death for a long while, seized control of military affairs, and tried to secure the succession for himself.

sentences.zh: 觀察判官李彬以為不可，當聽朝旨。

translations.literal: Investigation administrative aide Li Bin held that this could not be done and that they should await court orders.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation administrative aide Li Bin objected, insisting that they must await the court's decision.

sentences.zh: 紹基與群小等惡其異議，乃殺彬，紿奏云：「彬結構內外，謀殺都指揮使及行軍副使，自據城池，已誅戮訖，其妻子及諸房骨肉，尋令捕系次。

translations.literal: Shaoji and petty men hated his dissenting opinion and therefore killed Bin, falsely memorializing: "Bin plotted inside and outside, schemed to kill the overall commander and campaign deputy, seized the city on his own authority; he has already been executed; his wife, children, and all branches of kin will next be ordered captured and bound."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoji and his cronies, resenting Li Bin's opposition, killed him and submitted a false memorial: "Bin conspired inside and outside the command, plotted to murder the overall commander and campaign deputy, and seized the city on his own authority. He has been executed. His wife, children, and all collateral kin will be arrested next."

sentences.zh: 」太祖聞之，詔並釋之，仍令都送汝州安置。

translations.literal: " When Taizu heard this he edicted that all be released and still ordered them all sent to Ruzhou for placement.
translations.idiomatic: " When Taizu heard the report, he ordered all of them released and sent to Ruzhou for resettlement.

sentences.zh: 後朝廷令六宅使張仁謙往巡檢，紹基乃發喪以聞。

translations.literal: Later the court ordered Six Residences commissioner Zhang Renqian to go inspect; Shaoji then announced the mourning and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court sent the Six Residences commissioner Zhang Renqian to inspect the command. Only then did Shaoji announce the death and report it.

sentences.zh: 輟視朝兩日。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for two days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court audiences for two days in mourning.

sentences.zh: 折從阮，字可久，本名從遠，避漢高祖舊名下一字，故改焉。

translations.literal: Zhe Congruan, style name Kejiu, original name Congyuan; to avoid the taboo character below Han Gaozu's former name he therefore changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Congruan, courtesy name Kejiu, was originally named Congyuan. To avoid the taboo on the character in Han Gaozu's former name, he changed it.

sentences.zh: 代家雲中。

translations.literal: His family for generations was from Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived in Yunzhong for generations.

sentences.zh: 父嗣倫，為麟州刺史，累贈太子太師。

translations.literal: His father Silun was prefect of Linzhou and was repeatedly posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Silun had served as prefect of Linzhou and was posthumously awarded the title of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 從阮性溫厚，弱冠居父喪，以孝聞。

translations.literal: Congruan by nature was gentle and generous; upon reaching adulthood he dwelt in mourning for his father and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Congruan was gentle and generous by nature. When he came of age he observed mourning for his father and won renown for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗初有河朔之地，以代北諸部屢為邊患，起從阮為河東牙將，領府州副使。

translations.literal: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong first held the Hebei lands, because the northern Dai tribes repeatedly were frontier troubles he raised Congruan as Hedong yamen general and made him lead Fuzhou deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang first secured the Hebei region, the northern tribes beyond Dai repeatedly threatened the frontier. He appointed Congruan a Hedong yamen general and made him deputy commissioner of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 同光中，授府州刺史。

translations.literal: In Tongguang he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang period he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 長興初，入朝，明宗以從阮洞習邊事，加檢校工部尚書，復授府川刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing he entered court; Emperor Mingzong because Congruan thoroughly understood frontier affairs additionally made him acting Minister of Works and again appointed him prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changxing period he came to court. Emperor Mingzong, recognizing his thorough knowledge of frontier affairs, gave him the additional title of acting Minister of Works and reappointed him prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖起義，以契丹有援立之恩，賂以雲中、河西之地，從阮由是以郡北屬。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu raised righteous arms, because the Khitans had the grace of aiding his enthronement he bribed them with the lands of Yunzhong and Hexi; Congruan thereby came under the north of the command.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu rose in rebellion, he ceded Yunzhong and the Hexi region to the Khitans in gratitude for their support in his enthronement. Congruan's prefecture thus passed to Khitan control.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹欲盡徙河西之民以實遼東，人心大擾，從阮因保險拒之。

translations.literal: Shortly the Khitans wished to move all the people of Hexi to fill Liaodong; popular hearts were greatly disturbed; Congruan therefore held the strategic passes and resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans then sought to relocate the entire population of Hexi to populate Liaodong, throwing the region into turmoil. Congruan held the strategic passes and resisted.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝嗣位，北絕邊好，乃遣使持詔諭從阮令出師。

translations.literal: When Jin's young emperor succeeded, northern frontier friendship was severed; he then sent envoys bearing edicts instructing Congruan to order troops out.
translations.idiomatic: When the young emperor of Jin succeeded, relations with the northern frontier were broken off. The court sent envoys with edicts ordering Congruan to march out.

sentences.zh: 明年春，從阮率兵深入邊界，連拔十餘寨。

translations.literal: The next spring Congruan led troops deep into the frontier border and in succession captured more than ten stockades.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Congruan led his troops deep into the frontier and captured more than ten enemy stockades in succession.

sentences.zh: 開運初，加檢校太保，遷本州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was additionally made acting grand guardian and transferred to regimental commissioner of his native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaiyun period he was given the additional title of acting grand guardian and made regimental commissioner of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其年，兼領朔州刺史、安北都護、振武軍節度使、契丹西南面行營馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: That year he concurrently held prefect of Shuozhou, Protector-General Pacifying the North, military commissioner of the Zhenwu army, and overall adjutant of cavalry and infantry for the Khitan southwestern campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was given concurrent appointment as prefect of Shuozhou, Protector-General Pacifying the North, military commissioner of the Zhenwu army, and overall adjutant of the Khitan southwestern campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 漢祖建號晉陽，引兵南下，從阮率眾歸之。

translations.literal: When the Founder of Han established his title at Jinyang and led troops south, Congruan led the masses to submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Later Han proclaimed his reign at Jinyang and marched south, Congruan led his forces to join him.

sentences.zh: 尋升府州為永安軍，析振武之勝州並沿河五鎮以隸焉。

translations.literal: Shortly Fuzhou was elevated to the Yong'an army; Shengzhou of Zhenwu and five towns along the river were divided off to be subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fuzhou was elevated to the Yong'an army command, with Shengzhou from Zhenwu and five riverine towns placed under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 授從阮光祿大夫、檢校太尉、永安軍節度、府勝等州觀察處置等使，仍賜功臣名號。

translations.literal: Congruan was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting grand marshal, military commissioner of the Yong'an army, and commissioner for observation and disposition of Fu, Sheng, and other prefectures, and still bestowed a merit subject title.
translations.idiomatic: Congruan was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting grand marshal, military commissioner of the Yong'an army, and commissioner overseeing Fu, Sheng, and the surrounding prefectures, and was granted an honorific title for meritorious subjects.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年，加特進、檢校太師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyou he was given special advancement and acting grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyou he was given special advancement and the title of acting grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 明年春，從阮舉族入覲，朝廷命其子德扆為府州團練使，授從阮武勝節度使。

translations.literal: The next spring Congruan brought his whole clan to court for an audience; the court ordered his son Deyi regimental commissioner of Fuzhou and appointed Congruan military commissioner of Wusheng.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Congruan brought his entire clan to court. The court appointed his son Deyi regimental commissioner of Fuzhou and made Congruan military commissioner of Wusheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖受命，加同平章事，尋移鎮滑州，又改陜州。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the Mandate he was additionally made associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council; shortly he was transferred to garrison Huazhou and again changed to Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took power, Congruan was given the title of associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council. He was soon transferred to Huazhou and then to Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，授靜難軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second winter he was appointed military commissioner of the Jingnan army.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year he was appointed military commissioner of the Jingnan army.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，就加兼侍中，以年老上章請代，優詔許之。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne he was at once additionally made concurrent palace attendant; because of old age he submitted a memorial requesting replacement and a gracious edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Congruan was given the additional title of concurrent palace attendant. Citing his age, he petitioned for relief from command, and a gracious edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年冬，赴闕，行次西京，以疾卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: In the second winter of Xiande he went to court; on the way at the western capital he died of illness, age sixty-four at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Xiande he set out for court but died of illness at the western capital on the way, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 制贈中書令。

translations.literal: By decree he was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously awarded him the title of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王饒，字受益，慶州華池人也。

translations.literal: Wang Rao, style name Shouyi, was a man of Huachi in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rao, courtesy name Shouyi, was a native of Huachi in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父柔，以饒貴，累贈太尉。

translations.literal: His father Rou, because Rao was honored, was repeatedly posthumously granted Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rou was repeatedly posthumously awarded the title of Grand Marshal on account of Rao's eminence.

sentences.zh: 饒沈毅有才幹，始事晉高祖。

translations.literal: Rao was deep, resolute, and talented in ability; he first served Jin Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Rao was steady, resolute, and capable. He first entered the service of Jin Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 天福初，授控鶴軍使，稍遷奉國軍校，累加檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he was appointed commissioner of the Crane-Control army, shortly transferred to Fengguo army officer, and cumulatively given acting Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu period he was appointed commander of the Crane-Control army, soon promoted to an officer in the Fengguo army, and eventually given the additional title of acting Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 六年，從杜重威平常山，以功加檢校司空，遷本軍都校，領鄆州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Du Chongwei in pacifying Changshan, and for merit was additionally made acting Minister of Works, transferred to overall officer of his army, and concurrently prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Du Chongwei in the pacification of Changshan. For his achievements he was given the additional title of acting Minister of Works, made overall officer of his army, and appointed concurrent prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時安從進叛於襄陽，晉祖命高行周率兵討之，以饒為行營步軍都指揮使，賊平，授深州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time An Congjin rebelled at Xiangyang; Jin Gaozu ordered Gao Xingzhou to lead troops to suppress him and made Rao commander of campaign infantry; when the rebels were pacified he was appointed prefect of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When An Congjin rebelled at Xiangyang, Jin Gaozu ordered Gao Xingzhou to lead an army against him and appointed Rao commander of the campaign infantry. After the rebellion was crushed, Rao was made prefect of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復入為奉國都校，加檢校司徒，領欽州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he again entered service as overall Fengguo officer, was given acting Minister of Education, and concurrently held Qinzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he returned to court as overall officer of the Fengguo army, was given the additional title of acting Minister of Education, and appointed concurrent prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改本軍右廂都指揮使，領閬州團練使。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to commander of the right wing of his army and regimental commissioner of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made commander of the right wing of the Fengguo army and regimental commissioner of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉末，契丹據中原，漢祖建義於晉陽，尋克復諸夏，惟常山郡為契丹所據，時饒在其郡，乃與李筠、白再榮之儔承間竊發，盡逐其黨。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin the Khitans held the Central Plains; the Founder of Han raised righteous arms at Jinyang and shortly recovered the central lands; only Changshan commandery was held by the Khitans; at that time Rao was in that commandery; he then with Li Yun, Bai Zairong, and their kind seized an interval to rise in secret and completely drove out their faction.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jin dynasty the Khitans held the Central Plains. The founder of Later Han raised his banner at Jinyang and soon recovered the heartland, but Changshan remained in Khitan hands. Rao was then in that prefecture. He joined Li Yun, Bai Zairong, and others in a sudden uprising and drove out the Khitan faction entirely.

sentences.zh: 漢祖嘉之，授鄜州觀察留後，加光祿大夫，賜爵開國侯，復移授鎮國軍節度使，加檢校太傅。
