translations.literal: The Founder of Han commended this, appointed him acting regent of Fuzhou observation, gave Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, bestowed the enfeoffment Marquis Who Opens the State, again transferred him to military commissioner of the Zhenguo army, and gave acting grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: The founder praised his deed and appointed him acting regent of Fuzhou, granted him the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Marquis Who Opens the State, then transferred him to military commissioner of the Zhenguo army with the additional title of acting grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 國初，就加同平章事，賜推誠奉義翊戴功臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty he was at once additionally made associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council and bestowed the merit title Loyal, Sincere, Righteous, and Supporting.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Zhou dynasty he was given the title of associate director of the Secretariat with the Grand Council and the honorific merit title Loyal, Sincere, Righteous, and Supporting.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，以郊丘禮畢，加檢校太尉，移鎮貝州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, when the suburban altar rites were completed, he was additionally made acting grand marshal and transferred to garrison Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiande era, after the suburban altar rites were completed, he was given the additional title of acting grand marshal and transferred to Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，加兼侍中，改彰德軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded he was additionally made concurrent palace attendant and changed to military commissioner of the Zhangde army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Rao was given the additional title of concurrent palace attendant and appointed military commissioner of the Zhangde army.

sentences.zh: 滿歲受代，入奉朝請。

translations.literal: When his year was complete he accepted replacement and entered to hold court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After his term expired he was relieved of command and returned to court as a ceremonial attendant.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年冬，以疾卒於東京之私第，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth winter of Xiande he died of illness at his private residence in the Eastern Capital, age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year of Xiande he died of illness at his private residence in the Eastern Capital at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 追封巢國公。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Chao.

sentences.zh: 饒性寬厚，體貌詳雅，所蒞藩鎮，民皆便之。

translations.literal: Rao by nature was generous and tolerant, his bearing detailed and refined; in every frontier command he held, the people all found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Rao was generous and tolerant by nature, with a dignified and refined bearing. In every command he governed, the people found his rule agreeable.

sentences.zh: 每接賓佐，必怡聲緩氣，恂恂如也，故士君子亦以此多之。

translations.literal: Whenever he received guests and aides he always used a pleasant voice and gentle manner, respectful and deferential; therefore gentlemen also for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he received guests and subordinates he spoke in a pleasant, unhurried tone with respectful deference. For this reason men of cultivation held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 孫方諫，鄚州清苑縣人也。

translations.literal: Sun Fangjian was a man of Qingyuan county in Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fangjian was a native of Qingyuan County in Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 本名方簡，廣順初，以犯廟諱，故改焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Fangjian; at the beginning of Guangshun, because it violated the temple taboo, he therefore changed it.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Fangjian. At the start of the Guangshun era he changed it to avoid the imperial taboo.

sentences.zh: 定州西北二百里有狼山，山上有堡，邊人賴之以避剽掠之患，因中置佛舍。

translations.literal: Two hundred li northwest of Dingzhou was Wolf Mountain; on the mountain was a fort; frontier people relied on it to escape the trouble of raids and plunder, and therefore placed a Buddhist hall in its midst.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li northwest of Dingzhou stood Wolf Mountain, topped by a fortified stronghold where frontier people took refuge from raiders. A Buddhist hall was built there.

sentences.zh: 有尼深意者，俗姓孫氏，主其事，以香火之教聚其徒，聲言屍不壞，因復以衣襟，瞻禮信奉，有同其生。

translations.literal: There was a nun named Shenyi, secular surname Sun, who directed its affairs; by the incense-and-lamp teaching she gathered her followers; she proclaimed the corpse did not decay, and therefore again draped it with robe borders; those who gazed in worship believed and revered it as though it were still alive.
translations.idiomatic: A nun named Shenyi of the Sun clan directed the community. Through her teachings she gathered followers around the cult of incense and lamps. She claimed the corpse of her predecessor had not decayed, draped it again in robes, and her disciples worshipped it as though the body were still alive.

sentences.zh: 方諫即其宗人也，嗣行其教，率眾不食葷茹，其黨推之為寨主。

translations.literal: Fangjian was of her clan; he succeeded in carrying on her teaching, led the multitude not to eat meat or pungent vegetables, and his faction pushed him as stockade chief.
translations.idiomatic: Fangjian was a kinsman of her clan. He succeeded to her teachings, led his followers in abstaining from meat, and was chosen by the community as chief of the stronghold.

sentences.zh: 晉開運初，定帥表為邊界遊奕使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin Kaiyun the Ding commander memorialized him as frontier patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyun period the commander of Dingzhou memorialized the court to appoint him frontier patrol commissioner.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史·孫行友傳》：方諫懼主帥捕逐，乃表歸朝，因署為東北面招收指揮使，且賜院額曰勝福。

translations.literal: (《Song History》, Biography of Sun Xingyou: Fangjian feared the commander would capture and pursue him, and therefore memorialized submission to the court; he was thereby appointed northeastern recruitment commander and moreover granted the monastery plaque name Shengfu.)
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Song History》, biography of Sun Xingyou: Fangjian, fearing arrest by his commander, submitted to the court and was appointed northeastern recruitment commander. The monastery was granted the plaque name Shengfu.)

sentences.zh: 每契丹軍來，必率其徒襲擊之，鎧丈畜產所得漸多，人益依以避難焉。

translations.literal: Whenever Khitan armies came he always led his followers to strike them; armor, cloth, and livestock obtained gradually increased, and people increasingly relied on him to escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Khitan armies appeared he led his followers in attacks against them. The armor, cloth, and livestock they captured grew steadily, and more people came to rely on the stronghold for refuge.

sentences.zh: 易定帥聞於朝，因以方諫為邊界遊奕使，行友副之。

translations.literal: The Yi and Ding commander reported to court, and thereby Fangjian was made frontier patrol commissioner with Xingyou as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The commander of Yi and Ding reported to court, and Fangjian was appointed frontier patrol commissioner with Xingyou as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 自是捍禦侵軼。

translations.literal: From this they defended against raids and incursions.
translations.idiomatic: From that point they defended the frontier against raids and incursions.

sentences.zh: 多所殺獲，乘勝入祁溝關，平庸城，破飛狐砦，契丹頗畏之。）〉

translations.literal: They killed and captured many; pressing victory they entered Qigou Pass, pacified Pingyuan city, broke Feihu stockade, and the Khitans greatly feared them.)〉
translations.idiomatic: They killed and captured many enemies, advanced in victory through Qigou Pass, took Pingyuan, and stormed Feihu stockade, inspiring considerable fear among the Khitans.)〉

sentences.zh: 求請多端，因少不得志，潛通於契丹。

translations.literal: His requests were many and varied; because he was somewhat unsuccessful in his ambitions he secretly communicated with the Khitans.
translations.idiomatic: He made many demands of the court, and when they went largely unmet he secretly opened communications with the Khitans.

sentences.zh: 戎王之入中原也，以方諫為定州節度使，尋以其將耶律忠代之，改方諫雲州節度使。

translations.literal: When the barbarian king entered the Central Plains he made Fangjian military commissioner of Dingzhou; shortly he replaced him with his general Yelü Zhong and changed Fangjian to military commissioner of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor entered the Central Plains he appointed Fangjian military commissioner of Dingzhou, but soon replaced him with his general Yelü Zhong and reassigned Fangjian to Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 方諫恚憤，與其黨歸狼山，不受契丹命。

translations.literal: Fangjian was resentful and indignant; with his faction he returned to Wolf Mountain and would not accept Khitan orders.
translations.idiomatic: Fangjian, furious at the slight, returned to Wolf Mountain with his followers and refused to obey the Khitans.

sentences.zh: 漢初，契丹隳定州城壘，燒爇廬舍，盡驅居民而北，中山為之一空。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han the Khitans destroyed Dingzhou's walls and ramparts, burned dwellings, drove all residents north, and Zhongshan was thereby emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han period the Khitans demolished the walls of Dingzhou, burned the houses, and drove the entire population northward, leaving the region of Zhongshan deserted.

sentences.zh: 方諫自狼山率其部眾回保定州，上表請命，漢祖嘉之，即授以節鉞，累官至使相。

translations.literal: Fangjian from Wolf Mountain led his tribal masses back to secure Dingzhou, submitted a memorial requesting orders; the Founder of Han commended this and immediately granted him the military commissioner's banner and axe; through accumulated offices he reached commissioner and chancellor rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fangjian led his followers down from Wolf Mountain, reoccupied Dingzhou, and submitted a memorial pledging allegiance. The founder praised his loyalty, invested him with the commissioner's insignia, and eventually raised him to the rank of commissioner and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 太祖受命，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the Mandate he was additionally made concurrent palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took power, Fangjian was given the additional title of concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改華州節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to military commissioner of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to military commissioner of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其弟行友為定州留後，

translations.literal: The court made his younger brother Xingyou acting regent of Dingzhou,
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed his younger brother Xingyou acting regent of Dingzhou,

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史》云：行友上言，偵得契丹離合，願得勁兵三千，乘間平定幽州。

translations.literal: (《Song History》 says: Xingyou submitted a memorial reporting that he had detected Khitan divisions and unions and wished to obtain three thousand crack troops to seize an interval and pacify Youzhou.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Song History》 records: Xingyou memorialized that he had learned of divisions within the Khitan ranks and requested three thousand elite troops to seize an opportunity and pacify Youzhou.)

sentences.zh: 乃移方諫鎮華州，以行友為定州留後。）〉

translations.literal: Thereupon Fangjian was moved to garrison Huazhou and Xingyou was made acting regent of Dingzhou.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Fangjian was therefore transferred to Huazhou and Xingyou was made acting regent of Dingzhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 又以弟議為德州刺史，兄弟子侄職內廷者凡數人。

translations.literal: He also made his younger brother Yi prefect of Dezhou; brothers, sons, and nephews holding posts in the inner court numbered several men.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed his younger brother Yi prefect of Dezhou. Several of his brothers, sons, and nephews held posts within the inner court.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，史彥超代之，車駕駐蹕於並門，方諫自華覲於行在，從大駕南巡，以疾就醫於洛下。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded, Shi Yanchao replaced him; the imperial carriage halted at Bing Gate; Fangjian from Hua paid court at the traveling palace, followed the great carriage on the southern tour, and because of illness sought medical treatment below Luo.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Shi Yanchao replaced him at Huazhou. The emperor halted at Bing Gate, and Fangjian came from Hua to pay his respects at the traveling palace. He accompanied the imperial procession south but fell ill and sought treatment in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 尋授同州節度使，加兼中書令，未及赴任，以疾卒於洛陽，年六十二。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed military commissioner of Tongzhou and additionally made concurrent director of the Secretariat; before he could go to his post he died of illness at Luoyang, age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed military commissioner of Tongzhou and given the additional title of concurrent director of the Secretariat, but before he could take up the post he died of illness in Luoyang at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 輟視朝兩日，詔贈太師。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for two days; by edict he was posthumously granted Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court audiences for two days in mourning. An edict posthumously awarded him the title of Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔晉之季也，敵騎長驅，中原無主，漢祖雖思拯溺，未果圖南。

translations.literal: The historian says: In former days at the end of Jin, enemy cavalry drove far; the Central Plains had no master; although the Founder of Han thought to rescue the drowning, he had not yet succeeded in planning southward.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In the closing years of the Jin dynasty, enemy horsemen ranged freely across the land and the Central Plains had no sovereign. Though the founder of Later Han wished to rescue the realm from ruin, he had not yet succeeded in marching south.

sentences.zh: 趙暉首變陜郊，同扶義舉，漢之興也，暉有力焉，命以作藩，斯無愧矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Hui was first to change the Shan suburbs and together upheld the righteous rising; in Han's rise Hui had strength in it; appointing him to serve as frontier commander—this was without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hui was the first to rise in the Shan region and helped sustain the righteous cause. He contributed materially to the founding of Later Han, and his appointment as a frontier commander was well deserved.

sentences.zh: 守恩乘時效順，雖有可觀，好利殘民，夫何足貴！

translations.literal: Shou'en seized the time to show loyalty; although there was something to be seen in it, he loved profit and harmed the people—how could he be worth honoring!
translations.idiomatic: Shou'en seized the moment to submit, which had something to be said for it, but his greed and cruelty toward the people made him scarcely worthy of esteem.

sentences.zh: 允權、方諫，因版蕩之世，竊屏翰之權，比夫畫雲臺之功臣，何相去之遠也！

translations.literal: Yunquan and Fangjian, because of an age of upheaval, stealthily seized the power of frontier screens and bulwarks; compared with the merit subjects painted on the Cloud Terrace, how far apart they were!
translations.idiomatic: Yunquan and Fangjian seized frontier power in an age of turmoil. How far they fell short of the meritorious ministers whose portraits were painted on the Cloud Terrace!
